entry.title: Test
entry.content:
I joined my school’s electric racecar team as soon as I joined college. I became aerodynamics and frame lead, and eventually Chief Mechanical Engineer for the 25 person team. After two long years, we finally took the racecar to Michigan to race against other teams. I can’t say it went well, but it was a lot of work regardless.

Chief Engineer things

Aerodynamics

In my first semester of college I began learning basic Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations (while I was also learning CAD for the first time) and combined that with my rudimentary understanding of aerodynamics to design and test an aerodynamic package for the car. We ended up not using the wings in competition, but I definetly learned a lot in the process.

I also most of the carbon fiber bodywork and wings (that we never used) for the car. We used wet layups and vacuum bags for most parts.

We also did a resin infusion layup for the nosecone!

Frame

I taught myself basic Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in order to simulate the torsional rigidity of the steel spaceframe chassis.

entry.title: Mechatronics Robots
entry.content: I made two mechantronics robots in college. The first was The Dinosaur Lightning Tornado, a battlebot style robot that used IR sensors to stay within a ring and push opponents out. The robot is made of lasercut and 3D printed parts, and we even cast our own wheels from silicone. The micro-controller is an ATmega328P with assembly code. Grip is super important for the competiton, so I designed some wheels with a 3D printed core with super grippy silicone cast around it. I made a 3D printed mold for the silicone pour that could be easily cut off afterwards. I also lasercut a hub out of 1/4in steel.
